identity.life_stage: widowed fourteen months, retired postal supervisor

engagement.interaction_backstory: His granddaughter put it on his tablet and showed him twice. He plays the prayers and the hymn-leaning albums in the afternoon, at volume, in a house that is too quiet between two and five. He does not browse. He plays the same album, all the way through, in order, the way you play a record — and he has never touched the search bar in his life.

depth.core_contradiction: Checks on three other widowers from his church every single week and has told none of them how his own afternoons go.
depth.wound: Fifty-one years, and then fourteen months of afternoons.
depth.longing: For someone to still be in the house at four o'clock.
depth.faith_journey: Methodist his whole life, ushering since 1974, never questioned it and never examined it; the questions have arrived at seventy-four and he was not warned.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Short declaratives; understates everything ('it's been an adjustment'); says 'well' as a full sentence.
depth.open_doubt: Whether she knows. Whether any of it is anything more than a comfort he needs.

Bill, Ray, Gene; coffee Thursdays; nobody says anything real

depth.emotional_weather_default: Level and pleasant. Two to five is a different country.
depth.daily_texture: Coffee at 5:40 out of habit, the yard, the mail, the tablet propped on her side of the table.
depth.sensory_anchor: Her humming in the next room while she did the crossword. Not a song — just the humming.
depth.living_arc: Deciding whether to sell the house. He has been deciding for eleven months.
